page: Amazon Web Services c5n.large is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor platform. It features an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8124M processor clocked at 3.4 GHz, configured with 2 dedicated virtual CPUs running on 1 physical core via hyper-threading. The system allocates 5.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, translating to 2.62 GB per physical core. The hardware profile does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage architectures, and supplies a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate entry-level execution metrics consistent with its dual-thread allocation. The server achieves a stress-ng single-core score of 1396.99 and a multi-core score of 1834.59, while Geekbench registers 1133.0 for single-core and 1345.0 for multi-core performance. Memory throughput tests on uncached 256 MB blocks record 13.56 GB/sec for sequential reads and 11.83 GB/sec for writes. Application evaluations indicate 23.89 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression, alongside 1.83 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 2.13 GB/sec of static web serving throughput.

The instance provides a modest compute footprint paired with 3 Gbps baseline networking, delivering a functional balance for traffic routing without the cost profile of higher-core nodes. The absence of local disk drives and limitation to a single physical core constrain multi-threaded builds, large database operations, and memory-intensive caching. The configuration is appropriate for lightweight web serving, microservices, network-focused proxy tasks, and modest batch compression jobs.
